thread:
Alex G.: Heads-up: Nebula Health wants a multi-AZ perf validation + cost sketch before CTO call next Tue. Can we run a dual-region sweep and a failover scenario? Need numbers by EOD Fri.
Priya K.: Yes. Proposed test matrix: single-az baseline + cross-az (same region) + multi-region failover. Models: open-instruct-70b-ctx8k baseline and open-instruct-70b-quant 4-bit. Payload mix: 60% short (30-60 tok), 30% medium (150-250 tok), 10% long (600-1k tok).
Dan R.: Also measure cold-start cost when we trigger fallback to hosted pool. That was a showstopper last time. Track cold-start time and extra tokens generated during warm-up.
Alex G.: Good call. Also track TCP handshake time and TLS renegotiation spikes. At high connection churn the TLS handshakes were the culprit. Can infra-bot enable connection reuse and report handshake stats?
infra-bot: Connection pooling enabled on test runners. Metrics added: TLS handshake latency, conn reuse rate, active sockets, ephemeral port exhaustion. Tests scheduled: start=2026-11-05T08:30:00-07:00. Profiles: 300/800/1200/1800 qps. Each profile: 8m ramp, 20m sustain, 4m cooldown. Microburst: 45s @3x in minute 10 of sustain. Repeat cache-on and cache-off.
Priya K.: For KV cache: enable prefix caching for short prompts only. For long prompts, disable cache to emulate user docs. Compare throughput delta.
Dan R.: Security Q: customer asked for KMS attestation and key usage SLO (ops calls/sec). sec-qa-bot can you paste the short blurb we give them?
sec-qa-bot: SCP: SOC2 Type II (link: https://redwood.example/compliance), KMS: customer-managed Cloud KMS via VPC peering supported; typical in-path KMS add 6-12ms per call. Key usage SLO: 2000 KMS ops/s recommended for POC scale; we provide retry guidance. See docs: https://redwood.example/docs/kms-poc.
Alex G.: Pricing ask from the AE: produce a one-page burn estimate showing monthly cost at sustained qps, and a per-microburst overage table (per-minute cost at 2x/3x/5x). Also give delta for quant vs full-precision.
Priya K.: Note on quant: we expect throughput increase but batch sizing will change. Provide both per-token and per-request pricing examples.
Dan R.: Enterprise blockers to monitor during run: NAT gateway port limits; customer firewall rules causing idle connection drops; KMS throttling; fallback latency when routing to hosted fallback. Log any 429s from KMS.
Alex G.: Ops: include raw traces (jaeger), heap/gpu mem, batch size histogram, and a sample of model server logs around the microburst window.
infra-bot: Collected traces: jaeger span for request path, KMS span, connection handshakes. Dashboard: link will be posted after run. Agent run id=run-546781-01.
Priya K.: Runner CLI example (to share with prospect):
```
runner --endpoint=https://poc.redwood.example/generate \
  --profile=mixed-multi-az --ramp=8m --sustain=20m --burst=45s \
  --qps=1200 --payloads=payloads/nebula-mix.json --conn-pool=on
```
Dan R.: Measurement notes for report: synthetic generator (vegeta-llm), real-ish payload mix, cache toggles, and multi-az routing. Include definitions: p50/p95/p99, outage count, cold-start count, KMS 429s.
Alex G.: Can someone draft the results template? I want: TL;DR, run matrix, latency table p50/p95/p99 per profile, failover timeline with timestamps, cost estimates, security attachments. Keep it slide-friendly.
Priya K.: I'll draft and put a first-pass in this thread after ops posts numbers.
Dan R.: One more: add a small experiment to enable connection keepalive=60s vs 300s to see effect on ephemeral ports. Customers may prefer short keepalives.
infra-bot: Added keepalive variation. Run started (5467815001). Interim sample at end of each profile will be posted.
Alex G.: Thanks team — tagging @Priya K. and @Dan R. for follow-ups.
